newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho court jails three men for sedition.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho court jails three men for sedition.

text.p: Lesotho's High Court jailed three men for sedition on Wednesday after they broadcast a report on national radio saying they had overthrown the government.

Judge Michael Ramolibeli sentenced Matso Bolofo, 58, a former officer in the Lesotho police, former soldier Lelingoana Jonathan, 38, and Makara Sekautu, 64, the leader of the small opposition United Party, to four years in jail each.
The men were ordered to serve an effective two years in jail, as half of their sentences were suspended.
In his judgement, the judge said they "had the audacity to seek assistance from the armed forces so that their takeover of the government could proceed smoothly and peacefully".

The case arises from their involvement in a broadcast over Radio Lesotho on February 29 last year in which they declared the government had been overthrown, parliament dissolved and the constitution suspended.
The men were arrested by the mountain kingdom's army troops within minutes of the broadcast.
Lesotho's 78-year-old Prime Minister, Ntsu Mokhehle, has repeatedly been challenged since he won the first democratic polls in two decades in 1993.
Earlier this month, he was sacked by his own party amid accusations the country was drifting into lawlessness. The action followed a 11-day police mutiny which was eventually crushed by the army.
The monarch, King Letsie III, is expected to call a meeting of the southern African country's Council of State to deal with the leadership crisis.
